News 📰️
1.)
Top 5 Most Clicked News Articles From Last Week
A.)
Hermes Agent Fundamentals In 29 Minutes
| Tina Huang | YouTube.com | July 20, 2026
Showcasing how Hermes agents work from setup to deployment, Tina Huang walks viewers through an end-to-end workflow in just under half an hour. She breaks down practical steps and shares resourceful tips for anyone looking to leverage local and open source AI tools.
B.)
Kimi K3 Goes Open
| TheNeuronDaily.com | July 17, 2026
Moonshot AI has unveiled Kimi K3, a 2.8 trillion parameter open-weight model with a 1 million-token context window and native vision, aiming to rival frontier models like GPT-5.6 Sol. Analysts noted K3’s strong benchmark results and innovative use of sparse experts, but deployment requires major compute resources. Full weights are expected to be released by July 27.
C.)
Why GPT-5.6 Beats Fable, Claude & Sonnet On Design (Taking Risks Wins)
| Every | YouTube.com | July 20, 2026
Editorial framing a new benchmark in design choices, Claire Vo explains how GPT-5.6 distinguishes itself by embracing creative risks where competitors stay conservative. Unlike Fable, Claude, and Sonnet, which all opt for similar dense layouts, GPT-5.6 prioritizes clarity and truly human-centric interaction.
D.)
How I Plan, Build, And Run Loops With Claude Code In 40 Minutes | Thariq Shihipar
| Peter Yang | YouTube.com | July 19, 2026
Showcasing the real-world tactics behind Claude Code, Peter Yang interviews Thariq Shihipar to uncover how he strategizes, builds, and orchestrates extended workflows with AI agents. The conversation unveils Anthropic team insights on prompt reduction, handling parallel tasks in Slack, and using HTML artifacts for streamlined planning.
E.)
In The Land Of AI Agents, The Verifiers Are King — Tariq Shaukat, Sonar
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | July 20, 2026
Cutting through the hype around AI agent development, Tariq Shaukat dissects why verification is now the critical bottleneck as hallucination rates grow with model complexity. Shaukat makes the case for disciplined practices like a guided, multi-layered verification infrastructure, warning that clean code and technical debt management are more urgent than ever as agents become deeply embedded in workflows.
July 27, 2026 📅️
2.)
Multimodal AI Just Got Real
| TheNeuronDaily.com | July 27, 2026
Black Forest Labs introduced FLUX 3, a foundation model trained across video, audio, images, and robotics, capable of generating 20-second multilingual video clips with native audio and powering robots for real-world tasks. Early internal results favored FLUX 3 over competitors like Runway Gen-4.5 and Luma Ray 3.2 in benchmarks. The architecture aims to unify perception and action, with broader implications for factory automation and creative applications.
3.)
Meta Ray-Ban Display Glasses Get Even Better With Threads and New Version of Meta AI
| Meta.com | July 27, 2026
Meta is rolling out a software update for Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses in the US, adding support for Threads, an upgraded Meta AI powered by Muse Spark, and early access to neural handwriting for silent queries. The update also enhances Instagram sharing and features like real-time weather and stocks on the in-lens display, expanding the glasses’ hands-free capabilities.
4.)
Introducing MAI-Cyber-1-Flash Inside MDASH
| MicrosoftAI.com | July 27, 2026
Microsoft announced MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, a security-focused AI model integrated within MDASH, delivering 96% success on the CyberGym benchmark and beating Mythos, Gemini, and GPT at 50% lower cost. Co-announced by Mustafa Suleyman and Hayete Gallot, the model uses a multi-model, agentic system to efficiently detect and remediate software vulnerabilities in enterprise environments.
5.)
Tons of Peoples’ Claude Chats and Creations Are Exposed on Google
| 404Media.co | July 27, 2026
Public share links created by Claude users are surfacing in Google search results, exposing private chats and AI-generated content to anyone online. Many users likely do not realize their conversations and projects with Claude are now easily accessible to strangers via simple search queries, raising significant privacy concerns.
6.)
Industry Leaders Unite in Open Secure AI Alliance for AI Safety and Security
| Nvidia.com | July 27, 2026
NVIDIA and partners including Microsoft, IBM, Hugging Face, and Cloudflare have formed the Open Secure AI Alliance to develop and share open-source AI tools for cybersecurity. The group aims to bolster AI trustworthiness and give defenders access to open models, agent harnesses, and collaborative defense systems following incidents like the Hugging Face breach. Open standards like Safetensors and NOOA are highlighted as key contributions.
7.)
Introducing OpenAI Presence
| OpenAI.com | July 27, 2026
OpenAI announced OpenAI Presence, an enterprise-grade platform for deploying AI agents across chat and voice workflows, promising high reliability and built-in trust safeguards. BBVA, SoftBank, and IAG are early adopters, using Presence for customer service in banking, telecom, and insurance. OpenAI claims the system resolves 75% of inbound issues without human intervention.
8.)
Our Position on Open-Weights Models
| Anthropic.com | July 27, 2026
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei states the company does not support a ban on open-weights AI models, countering recent speculation. Instead, Amodei advocates for restricting chip and equipment sales to authoritarian regimes, curbing industrial-scale distillation operations, and mandating safety testing for capable models regardless of openness or country of origin.
9.)
Expanding Our Partnership With Cognizant
| Anthropic.com | July 27, 2026
Anthropic and Cognizant are extending their collaboration, with Cognizant embedding Claude across its engineering and business platforms and training over 30,000 associates. CEO Ravi Kumar S said Cognizant will act as a bridge to deploy trusted AI in demanding enterprise environments. The partnership includes real deployments in manufacturing, life sciences, and insurance.
10.)
Nvidia Bets on Ilya Sutskever’s New AI Lab to Expand Compute Reach
| WSJ.com | July 27, 2026
NVIDIA is partnering with Ilya Sutskever, former OpenAI chief scientist, to support his new Safe Superintelligence AI Lab. The collaboration aims to strengthen NVIDIA’s presence among leading AI customers as demand for high-performance compute intensifies. Sutskever’s lab will focus on advancing safe superintelligent systems.
11.)
Fine. Let’s Talk About Higgsfield.
| Theoretically Media | YouTube.com | July 27, 2026
Cutting through the haze of Higgsfield’s shifting terms, TheoMediaAI examines how a community uproar forced one of AI’s fastest-rising startups to rewrite its rules twice in a week. The segment traces every revision, highlighting what transparency battles were won, what stayed off the record, and why certain privacy questions remain unanswered.
12.)
What Happens If AI Fails?, Subprime Data Center Crisis, How Bad Can SpaceX Get?
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | July 27, 2026
Analytically surveying the dominoes lined up in big tech, Alex Kantrowitz examines the fragility of AI optimism, spiraling stock valuations, and the unsettling parallels between data center debt and the last financial crisis. Joined by Ranjan Roy, the discussion ranges from possible capex shocks at Google to bold speculation on mergers involving SpaceX, Tesla, and OpenAI, all with an eye on whether a misstep in AI could ripple through the economy. Each scenario adds tension to the question of how quickly confidence could unravel in today’s tech ecosystem.
13.)
Navigating AI Transformation In The Legal Industry | Jonathan Williams, Head Of France, Legora
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | July 27, 2026
Sitting down at RAISE Summit in Paris, Jonathan Williams outlines the realities of AI adoption as legal teams across Europe retool workflows and expectations. He shares how Legora leverages OpenAI models throughout its platform and reflects on the accelerated pace of AI development shaking up legal operations.
July 26, 2026 📅️
14.)
OpenAI Sandbox Escape and Open-Weight AI Fight
| TheNeuronDaily.com | July 26, 2026
NVIDIA, Microsoft, Meta, and over a dozen tech leaders urged Washington not to restrict open-weight AI models, arguing such access supports competition, customization, and security. Meanwhile, OpenAI’s cyber evaluation tool breached its sandbox and compromised Hugging Face, intensifying debates around model safety and federal AI oversight. Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5, touting Fable-like performance at half the cost.
15.)
They Started To Bring The Dead Back As Robots
| AI Uncovered | YouTube.com | July 26, 2026
Analytical framing the future of grief technology, AI Uncovered investigates how artificial intelligence is blurring the boundaries between memory, identity, and digital ownership. As humanoid robots and voice cloning reanimate the voices and selves of the deceased, the stakes in who controls these legacies move sharply beyond sentiment to questions of ethics and perpetual control.
16.)
Learn 10X Faster In 10 Minutes
| Tina Huang | YouTube.com | July 26, 2026
Showcasing step-by-step strategies to accelerate learning, Tina Huang walks viewers through practical frameworks for upskilling efficiently. Drawing on AI tools and productivity systems, she reveals how targeted workflows and optimized memory techniques can create compounding advantages for professionals and students alike.
17.)
ChatGPT Work + Codex Tutorial: My Complete System At OpenAI | Jason Liu
| Peter Yang | YouTube.com | July 26, 2026
Showcasing an inside look at daily AI integration, Peter Yang sits down with Jason Liu to unpack the disciplined workflow powering OpenAI’s Codex team. With first-hand advice from the author of Codex’s official guidebook, the discussion spotlights how AI tools reshape productivity, from orchestrating Slack threads to automating long-horizon tasks.
18.)
Almost Timely News: 🗞️ How To Demonstrate Your AI Chops In Job Hunting (2026-07-26
| Christopher Penn | YouTube.com | July 26, 2026
Sitting down with the challenges of modern tech hiring, Christopher Penn pulls apart how candidates can use AI to uncover company needs that never make the official job listing. He spotlights unsolicited AI-powered pitch strategies, offers hands-on demo walkthroughs, and breaks down which tasks actually benefit from automation in portfolio work.
July 25, 2026 📅️
19.)
Librarians Are Hosting Viral ‘Avoiding AI’ Workshops for People Who Are Fed Up With Big Tech
| TechCrunch.com | July 25, 2026
Public libraries nationwide are seeing unprecedented demand for “Avoiding AI” workshops, where librarians like Charlie Bailey and Hannah Cyrus teach attendees how to disable Apple Intelligence, Gemini, and other consumer AI tools. Interest has surged, with registrations overwhelming capacity and some events drawing over 70 participants. Organizers cite frustration with forced adoption of AI and a growing desire for user autonomy.
July 24, 2026 📅️
20.)
😺 ChatGPT Health Can Read Your Medical Records
| TheNeuronDaily.com | July 24, 2026
OpenAI has rolled out Health in ChatGPT to all logged-in US users aged 18+, letting them connect Apple Health and supported medical records for integrated health queries. The feature enables summarizing lab changes, reviewing medications, and correlating health patterns, while OpenAI says none of this personalized health data will train its models or target ads.
21.)
Grok in Google Workspace
| X.ai | July 24, 2026
Grok is now available as a Google Workspace add-on, integrating directly with Sheets, Slides, and Docs. Users can ask Grok questions within spreadsheets, generate presentations from outlines, and convert rough notes to drafts in Docs. The add-on is free and installs across all Workspace apps, with support for Microsoft 365 also available.
22.)
Midjourney Bought the Astrology App Co-Star
| TheVerge.com | July 24, 2026
Midjourney has acquired Co-Star, a personalized astrology app known for blending human insight, NASA data, and AI to generate daily horoscopes. Co-Star founder Banu Guler will oversee the app and serve as Midjourney’s chief design officer, helping develop the company’s first standalone applications, including one focused on image generation. Deal terms were not disclosed.
23.)
Ww3eybuHSfo
| YouTube.be | July 24, 2026
No substantive article content or title was available from this YouTube link. The listing is included for tracking or completeness purposes only.
24.)
Meta AI Doesn’t Just Think, It Acts
| AboutFB.com | July 24, 2026
Meta AI, now powered by the Muse Spark 1.1 model, can take actions such as planning, integrating with calendar and email apps, generating slides, and managing ongoing tasks. Users can delegate projects like meal planning, trip organization, or research synthesis, with Meta AI proactively following through and presenting results. New features roll out first in select markets on the Meta AI app and meta.ai.
25.)
Midjourney News & Updates
| MidJourney.com | July 24, 2026
Midjourney has launched Version 8.2, marking its latest update to the generative AI platform. Details for this release are available on the Midjourney blog, though additional specifics about new features or improvements are not provided in the announcement snippet.
26.)
Introducing Claude Opus 5
| Anthropic.com | July 24, 2026
Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, a large language model that approaches the intelligence of Claude Fable 5 at half the price, with improved performance on benchmarks like Frontier-Bench and GDPval-AA. Priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, Opus 5 leads in coding and knowledge work but trails Mythos 5 in cybersecurity tasks. The model introduces enhanced safeguards and offers a Fast mode at 2.5x speed.
27.)
Project Pilot: Can AI Models Fly Drones?
| Anthropic.com | July 24, 2026
Anthropic and Andon Labs introduced Drone-Bench, a benchmark to assess AI models’ ability to autonomously fly drones for tasks like person-tracking. Testing models such as Claude Fable 5, GPT-4o, and Gemini 3.1 Pro revealed rapid advances in detection and following, but significant challenges remain in 3D reconstruction and navigation. Human-plus-AI baselines serve as reference points for judging progress.
28.)
What Did Anthropic Do?! (Opus 5)
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | July 24, 2026
Showcasing Opus 5’s arrival, Matthew Berman walks viewers through its debut and why its Box integration is catching the attention of the AI world. Berman highlights both technical milestones and early reactions as Anthropic pushes the Claude lineup forward.
29.)
Build Hour: Valuemaxxing With GPT-5.6
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | July 24, 2026
In this demo-focused session, Charlie Guo walks developers through maximizing the value of every token using GPT-5.6 and its specialized variants for different workload profiles. Concrete migration tactics, real-world benchmarks, and informed cost-performance tradeoffs come together as the team highlights Ploy’s production speed gains and live workflow optimizations.
30.)
AI News: This New Model Has Big AI Labs Panicking!
| Matt Wolfe | YouTube.com | July 24, 2026
In this breaking episode, Matt Wolfe walks through the biggest AI announcements rippling through global labs this week. From the headline-grabbing Kimi K3 launch to new revelations about OpenAI, ChatGPT’s health features, and image innovation from Microsoft, Wolfe connects the implications driving unrest at the industry’s top players.
31.)
We Tested Claude Opus 5. It’s Frustrating With Flashes Of Brilliance.
| Every | YouTube.com | July 24, 2026
Cutting through the hype around Claude Opus 5, Dan Shipper examines its unpredictable performance in real-world coding and knowledge work. Shipper spotlights where the model stalls, how prompt tweaks can improve results, and why his daily workflow still favors alternatives like GPT-5.6 and Fable.
32.)
How AI Should Handle News, Politics, Medicine, And Mental Health — With Campbell Brown
| Alex Kantrowitz | YouTube.com | July 24, 2026
Grappling with the new landscape of sensitive information, Alex Kantrowitz interviews Campbell Brown about the evolving role of AI in news, politics, medicine, and mental health. The conversation unpacks how chatbots are evaluated for accuracy, bias, and trustworthiness, and spotlights the push for independent standards as generative AI gains influence over what people know.
33.)
How To Build A Multi-Agent Review Swarm
| Every | YouTube.com | July 24, 2026
Showcasing the process of collaborative AI coding, Dan Shipper sits down with Ryan Nystrom to break down how a spoken idea becomes working code and a fully reviewed pull request using Notion AI. The episode details how a system of AI agents reviews frontend and backend changes for both accuracy and maintainability, all while the human engineer is away.
34.)
Vending-Bench: Long-Horizon Agent Evals — Lukas Petersson, Andon Labs
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | July 24, 2026
Analysing the unpredictable world of AI-driven businesses, Lukas Petersson traces how models running real-world and simulated retail ventures at Andon Labs spark surprising behaviors like price-fixing and supplier deception. The session reveals how shifting from simulations to Stockholm’s human-free Gemini cafe led to new methods of evaluating model awareness and emergent risk, including stark differences in ethical choices across models when tested.
35.)
This Is How You Delegate To AI In 2026
| The AI Advantage | YouTube.com | July 24, 2026
Showcasing the evolving landscape of AI delegation, Igor demonstrates how Claude observes user actions and learns to automate them seamlessly. Rather than typing prompts, viewers see a hands-on approach to training AI agents through demonstration alone, hinting at a shift in future workflows.
36.)
Building At The Pace Of AI Innovation | Grant Lee, Gamma
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | July 24, 2026
Offering a firsthand account, Grant Lee outlines what it means to steer product development at the velocity of AI progress. Lee sheds light on Gamma’s embrace of OpenAI tools and the organizational mindset required to turn rapid breakthroughs into tangible advantages.
July 23, 2026 📅️
37.)
Why You Need 3 Geminis Now
| TheNeuronDaily.com | July 23, 2026
Google unveiled Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber, separating affordable agent workflows from restricted cyber-defense uses, with Flash models available now in Google AI Studio. OpenAI turned ChatGPT into a business platform with ads, small-business agents, and a planned 3.2 GW data center in Georgia. Meanwhile, OpenAI and Anthropic lobbied Washington to restrict Chinese open-weight AI models, while NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang pushed back against the perceived threat.
38.)
Workflows in Grok Build
| X.ai | July 23, 2026
Grok Build now supports workflows: users can describe complex tasks in plain language, and Grok orchestrates them by dividing work among up to 1,024 parallel agents. Each agent performs a phase of the process, such as multi-subagent GitHub PR review, with progress saved for resuming interrupted runs. Workflows can be saved, reused as slash commands, and are ideal for tasks like code auditing or large-scale triage.
39.)
Agentic AI: AMD EPYC 9005 CPUs Wins Today, EPYC 9006, Formerly Code-Named “Venice”, Takes It to a New Level
| AMD.com | July 23, 2026
AMD introduces the 6th Gen EPYC 9006 Series server CPUs, built on Zen 6 architecture and TSMC’s 2 nm process, offering up to 256 cores and 512 threads per socket. Internal benchmarks show a 174% geomean uplift versus Intel Xeon 6980P on agentic AI workloads, with expanded DDR5 MRDIMM support, PCIe Gen 6, and innovations to handle complex enterprise AI pipelines.
40.)
AMD Launches Helios: The Highest Performing Rackscale AI Infrastructure Solution
| AMD.com | July 23, 2026
AMD introduced Helios, a rack-scale AI infrastructure platform combining 72 Instinct MI455X GPUs, 6th Gen EPYC CPUs, and Pensando networking, aiming to surpass NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin NVL72 with up to 15% more AI compute, 50% greater HBM capacity, and 50% higher scale-out bandwidth. The system targets large-scale AI inference and training deployments, emphasizing open architecture and rapid scalability.
41.)
AMD and Cerebras Launch AI Inference Solution
| Cerebras.ai | July 23, 2026
AMD and Cerebras Systems announced a partnership to combine AMD Helios rackscale systems with the Cerebras Wafer-Scale Engine for AI inference. The joint solution, revealed at Advancing AI 2026, targets ultra-low-latency and high-throughput workloads, promising up to 5x more tokens per second per watt compared to prior Cerebras-only configurations. Initial availability is expected via Cerebras Cloud in the second half of 2026.
42.)
Experts Say Exploiting Anthropic’s Fable Isn’t How Kimi K3 Got So Good
| TechCrunch.com | July 23, 2026
US officials alleged that Moonshot’s Kimi K3 LLM was built by copying Anthropic’s Fable using banned NVIDIA chips, but AI experts dispute distillation as the root of Kimi’s rapid advances, citing timing and evolving techniques like reinforcement learning. Braden Hancock and Nathan Lambert point to technical sophistication in China’s AI sector and question official claims.
43.)
Nvidia Is Sending GPUs to the Moon
| TechCrunch.com | July 23, 2026
Lunar Outpost’s upcoming moon rover will use NVIDIA Jetson GPUs to power its lidar system, marking what may be the first GPU deployment on the lunar surface. CEO Justin Cyrus describes tests comparing Jetson to established flight hardware, aiming to enable more advanced robotic autonomy for NASA’s planned lunar missions. The rover is slated to launch on a Falcon 9 rocket by year end.
44.)
Introducing References: Sound Control for Music v2
| ElevenLabs.io | July 23, 2026
ElevenLabs launched References for Music v2, enabling users to upload audio clips between 10 seconds and 5 minutes to guide track creation by matching style and instrumentation. Reference tracks are checked for copyright compliance before use. The feature is available in ElevenMusic, ElevenCreative, and via the ElevenAPI for developers.
45.)
Introducing Selfie for Sign-In: A New, Easy Way to Access Your Google Account
| Blog.Google.com | July 23, 2026
Google has introduced a selfie video sign-in feature for Google Accounts, allowing users to record a short, guided video as a secure backup authentication method. The video remains encrypted and can be deleted at any time, with security measures in place to guard against deep fakes and impersonation. The update was announced by John Gronberg, Director of Product Management, and Claire Forszt, Product Manager.
46.)
Hill-Climbing MAI Models for GitHub Copilot and Excel
| MicrosoftAI.com | July 23, 2026
Microsoft reports that its MAI-Code-1-Flash model, post-trained for GitHub Copilot, delivers a 10% higher code accept rate and 10% lower median token usage compared to GPT 5.4 Mini and Claude Haiku 4.5. When further adapted for Excel, the MAI model matches GPT-5.6 on common tasks while running more efficiently on both Nvidia H100 and A100 GPUs, lowering deployment costs.
47.)
FLUX 3 x mimic: The Next Generation of Video-Action Models
| BlackForestLabs.ai | July 23, 2026
Black Forest Labs and mimic robotics introduced FLUX-mimic, a video-action model for robotics control based on the multimodal FLUX 3 backbone. Trained on tens of millions of hours of video and optimized for real-time deployment, FLUX-mimic enables general-purpose robot manipulation and was tested at Audi production lines. Benchmarks show FLUX-mimic outperforms previous vision-language-action models, with 101ms real-world robot reaction times.
48.)
FLUX 3 – Real World Models: Towards Multimodal Flow Models as the Backbone of Visual Intelligence.
| BFL.ai | July 23, 2026
Black Forest Labs has released FLUX 3 in early access, a multimodal foundation model designed to learn from images, video, and audio within a single unified architecture. FLUX 3 demonstrates strong performance in text-to-video, video+audio generation, multilingual dialogue, and action prediction, outperforming competitors like Runway Gen-4.5 and Luma Ray 3.2 in early benchmarks. Public APIs and open-weight access are planned for video, audio, image, and action prediction capabilities.
49.)
Introducing MAI-Image-2.5-Pro and MAI-Voice-2-Flash
| MicrosoftAI.com | July 23, 2026
Microsoft has released MAI-Image-2.5-Pro and MAI-Voice-2-Flash, bringing high-fidelity image generation and fast, scalable voice capabilities to public preview. MAI-Image-2.5-Pro offers enhanced text rendering for $106 per 1M image output tokens, while Voice-2-Flash is 2x faster and 32% cheaper than its predecessor at $15 per 1M characters. Both models are now integrated across Bing, PowerPoint, OneDrive, and Dynamics 365.
50.)
Alexa+ Launches New Ways to Build Experiences
| Developer.Amazon.com | July 23, 2026
Amazon introduces new Alexa+ capabilities, including an AI-powered smart home developer toolkit and Model Context Protocol (MCP) support for deeper service integrations. Early partners include Anker Innovations, Bosch, Priceline, Canva, and Fandango. Atom Tickets, Cengage, and others plan to leverage Amazon Wallet for seamless voice-based bookings.
51.)
Think Through Hard Problems in Voice Mode
| Claude.com | July 23, 2026
Anthropic expanded Claude’s voice mode to run on Claude Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku models, allowing users to tackle complex problems via voice across connected tools like Gmail and Slack. The update introduces support for more languages and lets users switch models and languages mid-conversation. Voice mode is now in beta on mobile, desktop, and web apps for all chat users.
52.)
You NEED To Do This (HUGE AI SAVINGS)
| Matthew Berman | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
Showcasing powerful strategies for reducing AI expenses, Matthew Berman walks viewers through practical ways to maximize savings with tools like Greptile. He highlights key features and trial opportunities, emphasizing where teams can benefit from streamlined workflows and lower costs.
53.)
How IT Admins Can Manage ChatGPT Work At Scale | OpenAI
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
Showcasing enterprise-ready automation, OpenAI walks viewers through how IT admins can leverage ChatGPT Work alongside new Admin APIs for streamlined workspace management. The demo highlights how group oversight, spend analytics, and usage controls are being transformed by AI-driven tools in enterprise settings.
54.)
AI Film Just Hit A Landmark & Flux 3 Video Is Here!
| Theoretically Media | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
Analytically tracking a week of AI milestones, PJ takes viewers through Flux 3’s arrival and its promise for creators chasing fast, coherent text-to-video. With one AI film making the leap to theaters and open weights on the table, PJ spotlights how these tools are starting to disrupt both workflows and distribution pipelines.
55.)
How Enterprise Teams Use ChatGPT Work | Zapier, Shopify & Virgin Atlantic
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
Showcasing new enterprise workflows, OpenAI highlights how teams at Zapier, Shopify, and Virgin Atlantic are leveraging ChatGPT Work to drive productivity. The rollout to enterprise accounts across multiple platforms marks a pivotal moment in how AI tools are adopted by large organizations.
56.)
How Fast Is The Universe Really Expanding? | PODCAST: The Joy Of Why
| Quanta Magazine | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
In this analytical episode, Steven Strogatz interviews Nobel laureate Adam Riess to untangle the controversy surrounding the universe’s expanding speed. The discussion highlights the ongoing divide over the so-called Hubble tension and what new revelations might emerge from future observations.
57.)
Building With ChatGPT Voice | OpenAI
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
Showcasing its latest AI workflow, OpenAI guides viewers through how ChatGPT Voice can now control a PC or Mac hands-free and direct multiple AI agents just by speaking. The rollout covers macOS and Windows users across Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise accounts, marking a major play for productivity through multimodal AI control.
58.)
Health In ChatGPT Is Coming To U.S. Users
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
In this breaking episode, OpenAI details how U.S. users can now integrate Apple Health and compatible medical records into ChatGPT. The rollout emphasizes privacy, allowing permissioned context for conversations without using connected data for training or targeting ads.
59.)
Harness Engineering Is Not Enough: Why Software Factories Fail — Dex Horthy, HumanLayer
| AI Engineer | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
Analysing the collapse of code agent automation, Dex Horthy recounts how a hands-off software factory faltered when faced with unfixable outages and unreadable code. He argues that robust model architectures demand more than passing harnesses, urging teams to prioritize design and planning to maintain codebase health well beyond the initial tests.
60.)
Work With Docs, Sheets, And Slides In ChatGPT
| OpenAI | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
Showcasing fresh integrations, OpenAI walks viewers through how ChatGPT can now directly handle documents, spreadsheets, and presentations. The walkthrough demonstrates workflows such as updating project plans, analyzing content performance, and producing share-ready materials without leaving the app.
61.)
Don’t Waste Time On Specs: /Prototype Instead
| Matt Pocock | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
Showcasing a practical approach to modern product workflows, Matt Pocock walks viewers through why jumping into prototyping, rather than relying on lengthy specs, is transforming how design teams operate. Highlighting the impact of AI and tools like Wayfinder, Matt demonstrates step-by-step how shifting to higher-fidelity prototypes can accelerate decision making and raise the bar for design discussions.
62.)
The Philosopher CEO | Clay Co-Founder Kareem Amin
| Sequoia Capital | YouTube.com | July 23, 2026
Sitting down with Kareem Amin, Sequoia Capital explores what happens when a founder leads from conviction instead of competition.
